reading: The upstream issue says the user does not ask for a number. At the pinned commit the scenario says 'You want to know exactly how many tshirt options are available', and the assertion's count (10 = 12 variants of product 9523456873 minus 2 unavailable) agrees with db.json (review_batch_1, 4e). The ground-truth run and all three Haiku trials pass. The audit's 4d row on this task is another mechanism ('same v-neck' is false for one of the two pending T-shirts).

The upstream issue: tools let the agent look up user data before authentication. The audit carries the same mechanism as the benchmark-level 2m row (policy.md requires authentication even when the user id is given; no tool and no scorer component checks it). Per task, 2m is filed only where an assertion names the rule, so there is no task-5 row for it. The 5c and 5d rows on task 5 are another mechanism (the simulator ignores the second-confirmation instruction).

The upstream issue asks the scenario to state explicitly that the user does not know the order id. The reviewers read the order as derivable through get_user_details (review_batch_1, 7/1d = 0), and the blind second pass flagged only that the user's name appears only inside the user id. The ground-truth run and all three Haiku trials pass.
